newsitem.title: UK: Sugar freight market quiet in routine business.
newsitem.headline: Sugar freight market quiet in routine business.

text.p: Sugar freight business was relatively calm on Tuesday with routine orders reported and little firm tonnage, shipbrokers said.

Mauritius Sugar Syndicate (MSS) fixed 13,200 tonnes of bulk sugar from Port Louis to Lisbon at stg 13.50, which shipbrokers said was stg 0.25 lower than the rate acheived for the previous similar fixture.

Other firmer business included 14/15,000 tonnes of bagged sugar from south Brazil to Red Sea with options of east Africa and Karachi for 5/15 November and 12,500/13,500 tonnes in bags from Buenaventura to Colombo for the same dates.
E D & F Man quoted for 20,000 tonnes of bulk sugar for 15/20,000 tonnes in bulk from Paranagua to Morocco with Egyptian Mediterranean and Black Sea options.
Genoc was in the market for a prompt 5,000-tonne bagged parcel from northern France to Algeria.
Shipbrokers said Brazilian shippers SIMAB quoted for 14,000 tonnes of bagged sugar from Recife to Lagos for 7/12 November.
